title: The affordance surface offers deployment.set_target, so the binding control has something to spend
description:
PRODUCER ROW filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-06 at governor-afbde490's 13:50Z direction (the "no target-binding UI" gap in worker-f72a1438's audit of task-84cd2e55aae942cf8d56657308215fde).

THE GAP IS THE OFFER, NOT THE CONTROL - and the card already says so in its own source. `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-deployments.tsx:189-192`:
  // set_target affordance is offered, so a control here would have none to spend.
  `Bind a target for ${view.environment} first, with deployment.set_target.`
  + " This screen cannot bind one yet, so it has to be bound outside the"
and `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/deploy-port.ts:29` records the same measurement: "excluding tests returns zero. So a `deployment.set_target` dispatch has no affordance to [spend]".
So the browser is not missing a button by oversight - it is correctly refusing to render a control that would have no affordance to spend. THE PRODUCER IS THE MISSING PIECE, and this row is it.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS task-2cedb26a598540bd9bab17046592a7bb (the `deployment.deploy` per-goal offer, planned 2026-09-06). Read that row's plan first and follow it: the same generic emission at affordance-read.ts:282-284, the same `aggregateIdFor` fallthrough in bootstrap-sequence.ts that targets the PROJECT, and the same requirement to assert the target id BY VALUE against what the card matches.

THE GRANULARITY DIFFERS FROM THE DEPLOY OFFER, AND THAT IS THE DECISION THIS ROW MUST MAKE. `deployment.set_target`'s payload keys are `["environment", "network", "sshTarget", "url"]` (daemon-command-payload-keys.ts:165) and the durable target is keyed `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>` (deploy-target-contracts.ts:84) - so unlike `deployment.deploy`, whose environment is chosen at dispatch from a single goal-scoped offer, BINDING is a per-(project, environment) act. Decide whether the offer is goal-scoped with the environment in the payload, or one per environment, and state it in a comment at the offer site the way task-2cedb26a requires. Do not leave the browser to infer it.

WITHHOLDING IS THE INVERSE OF THE DEPLOY OFFER'S. A deploy offer is withheld when NO target is bound; a set_target offer is what an operator needs precisely THEN. Say what the rule is - it is not "withheld when already bound", because rebinding is legitimate.

NOT IN SCOPE: the binding control itself (the parent task-84cd2e55 owns the card), the deploy offer (task-2cedb26a), and how set_target executes (task-358b6ec8).
definitionOfDone: The affordance read offers `deployment.set_target`, targeted at the aggregate the consuming control will match, asserted BY VALUE on `targetAggregateId` against the production surface read - not a hand-built frame. `git grep -c "set_target" -- apps/control-room/src` excluding tests currently proves zero affordance to spend; that count must become nonzero through a real offer.

THE GRANULARITY DECISION IS MADE AND WRITTEN DOWN in a comment at the offer site: goal-scoped with the environment in the payload, or one offer per environment. The payload keys are ["environment","network","sshTarget","url"] and the durable target is keyed per (project, environment) - state which authority the offer carries and how the environment is determined at dispatch. A test asserts the decided shape.

THE WITHHOLDING RULE IS STATED AND ASSERTED, and it is NOT the deploy offer's rule inverted carelessly: an operator needs set_target precisely when nothing is bound, and REBINDING an already-bound environment is legitimate. Say what withholds the offer, if anything, and assert both the offered and withheld cases as an offered-kind SET.

Every asserting consumer of the affordance surface is censused WHOLE-TREE and named with a verdict. `git grep -ln "affordance|nextAllowed|offered" -- 'tests/**'` returned 33 files at filing (tests/e2e, tests/integration, tests/security, tests/fault) plus four affordance test files under apps/daemon/src/http - all invisible to a package-scoped grep. Say which needed an arm and why the others did not.

MUTATION DRILL, quoted with its failing line: target the offer at the project aggregate instead of the decided key and confirm the by-value arm goes RED. Restore per global rail 13 - back the path up out of tree, restore from the backup rather than `git checkout --`, prove by sha256 in a separate call.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file; if the census found asserting consumers under tests/**, say which lanes you ran (`pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm test:integration`) and which you did not.
taskRails: THE OFFER IS THE MISSING PIECE, NOT THE BUTTON. goal-deployments.tsx:189-192 correctly refuses to render a control with no affordance to spend; producing the offer is what unblocks it.
FOLLOW task-2cedb26a's PLAN - same emission site, same fallthrough, same by-value assertion discipline. A second pattern for the same problem is a second thing to reason about.
STATE THE GRANULARITY, DO NOT LEAVE IT TO THE BROWSER. Binding is per (project, environment); decide what the offer carries and write it at the offer site.
REBINDING IS LEGITIMATE. Do not withhold the offer merely because a target is already bound.
CENSUS THE WHOLE TREE, not just apps/daemon - 33 files under tests/** assert on this surface and none is visible to a package-scoped grep.
DO NOT CHANGE HOW set_target EXECUTES (task-358b6ec8) OR BUILD THE CONTROL (parent task-84cd2e55).

THE ARMS FIRST, AND THEY MUST BE RED BEFORE ANY PRODUCTION EDIT (the governor's 20:30Z point (c), and the reason the last attempt shipped a design that dispatch refused). THE CONTRACT THESE ARMS PIN: one `deployment.set_target` offer PER ENVIRONMENT, each with `targetAggregateId = deployTargetAggregateId(projectId, environment)` — the aggregate the setter actually fences — and `expectedVersion = versionOf(ledger, thatKey)`. Import `deployTargetAggregateId` from ../deployment/deploy-target-contracts.js.
(a) BY VALUE, ALL THREE: in the existing module-level world (`surface()`), assert the set_target offers as an EXACT ORDERED list of {targetAggregateId, expectedVersion} tuples: `deploy-target:proj-affordance:preview`, `:production`, `:verify`, each at expectedVersion 0. Not a shape match, not a `toContain` — an id that merely looks right renders nothing in the card.
(b) NO PROJECT-TARGETED OFFER SURVIVES: assert `offers.filter(o => o.commandKind === "deployment.set_target" && o.targetAggregateId === PROJECT)` equals []. Paired with (a) that is the SET, not a subset (DoD 3) — the two-offers hazard is exactly what makes a surface bug read as a UI bug.
(c) THE ARM THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THE ORIGINAL DEFECT, and the one that matters most: build a DEDICATED world (openBootstrapStore + driveThrough, the way the `surfaceWithTargets` describe does — do NOT commit a binding into the shared module-level store, later tests in this file depend on its state). Commit ONE REAL `deployment.set_target` for `preview` at expectedVersion 0 through the production dispatch. Re-read the surface. Assert the preview offer's expectedVersion now equals `versionOf(ledger, deployTargetAggregateId(projectId, "preview"))` AND is 1, that `production`/`verify` are still 0 — independent versions on one surface — and then SPEND the preview offer: dispatch a rebind carrying that exact expectedVersion and assert `ok === true`. THE SUCCESSFUL DISPATCH IS THE EVIDENCE. A version arm that only compares numbers would have passed the falsified plan too.
(d) WITHHOLDING, PREREQUISITE-QUALIFIED (DoD 3): in a world before `project.activate`, assert ZERO set_target offers and that the single chain step is `{status: "BLOCKED", missing: ["project.activate"]}`. Rebinding an already-bound environment is legitimate, so after activation the offer is present in BOTH the never-bound and the already-bound case — (a) and (c) are those two halves. State in a comment that nothing ADDITIONAL withholds it once the bootstrap prerequisite is met; "nothing withholds it" is false and QA reads it literally.
(e) UPDATE THE ONE EXISTING ASSERTING CONSUMER — affordance-read.test.ts:1364-1379, `withholds the offer entirely when no environment has a bound target`. Its `.filter(kind => kind.startsWith("deployment.")).sort()).toEqual(["deployment.set_target"])` goes red on cardinality the moment there are three. Replace the kind-only list with the exact per-environment {targetAggregateId, expectedVersion} tuple list (the governor's 20:30Z (b): exact tuples, not Set-away). KEEP its intent verbatim — the deploy offer is withheld while the way to FIX it is still offered.
(f) DO NOT EDIT the `cards the non-planning dispatch roster and offers exactly its READY tuples` arm at :521-565. Its `offered` vs `expected` arrays are compared with cardinality, and step 4's splice is what keeps them equal — three offers against three READY steps. VERIFY it still passes rather than assuming; if it reds, the splice is missing, which is the whole point of that arm.
RUN THE FILE AND QUOTE THE FAILING LINES. These arms MUST be red now.

Body:

NAME POLICY = A UNION OF TWO DURABLE SOURCES, no invented names (task rail 6, governor 20:30Z (a)): (i) `ENVIRONMENT_NAMES` from ../environment/environment-contracts.js — the closed roster the deployments read already renders (goal-deployment-read.ts:42), which is what makes the FIRST browser bind possible; (ii) the suffixes of `store.enumerateAggregateIdsByPrefix(deployTargetAggregateId(projectId, ""))` — every environment ALREADY bound durably, including an out-of-roster name the regex setter admitted. 2. ORDER IS DETERMINISTIC AND ASSERTED: ENVIRONMENT_NAMES order first, then the durable-only extras ascending (enumerate already returns sorted ascending). Dedupe. Step 2(a) compares an ORDERED list, so a Set with nondeterministic iteration order is not acceptable.
3. VERSION IS READ, NEVER FABRICATED: `versionOf(ledger, deployTargetAggregateId(projectId, environment))`. `versionOf` on an aggregate with no events is 0, which is precisely the correct first-bind expectedVersion — so first bind and rebind need no branch. If a version cannot be read from a durable aggregate there is no offer to mint; an invented one refuses at dispatch in front of an operator, which is worse than no offer.
WRITE THE GRANULARITY DECISION AS A COMMENT AT THIS SITE (DoD 2). State: ONE OFFER PER ENVIRONMENT, not one per goal, because `NextAllowedCommand` (runtime-affordance.ts:18-28) carries a SINGLE SCALAR `expectedVersion` behind closed AFFORDANCE_REQUIRED/AFFORDANCE_OPTIONAL rosters, so an environment->version map is not expressible without a shared-contract rotation (epic rail 1, out of scope), while `deploy-target:<projectId>:<environment>` versions move INDEPENDENTLY. State the consumer contract that follows: the card constructs `deployTargetAggregateId(projectId, environment)` for the row it is rendering and spends THAT offer, so the payload's `environment` and the fenced aggregate agree BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by convention — it must not parse the environment back out of the id. Note also why this lives here and not in `resolvePlanningOffers`: that resolver runs PER GOAL and concatenates without dedupe (affordance-planning-offers.ts), so a mint there would emit N identical offers for N goals; minting once per project per poll is the dedupe, by construction.

THE MEASUREMENT THE LAST TWO ATTEMPTS MISSED, and the one that closes the first-bind hole: affordance-read.ts ALREADY imports ENVIRONMENT_NAMES (line 14) and already iterates it at :277 and :404. The closed roster ["preview","production","verify"] (environment-contracts.ts:29) is at the offer site today. So the name policy needs no invention and no new provisioning source. NAME POLICY = ENVIRONMENT_NAMES (makes the first browser bind possible) UNION the suffixes of store.enumerateAggregateIdsByPrefix(deployTargetAggregateId(projectId,"")) (covers an out-of-roster name, which IS reachable: the setter admits environments BY REGEX at deploy-receipt-contracts.ts:139, not by the roster - environment-contracts.ts:127 isEnvironmentName is a DIFFERENT function and is not on the setter's path). planningNotes.risks:
1. THE SPLICE IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT COSMETIC. Push three offers without splicing the generic chain step and affordance-read.test.ts:555-566 reds on cardinality. That arm is also the DoD-3 set-equality guard, so drill (iii) must show it biting.
2. NEVER TAKE `expectedVersion` FROM A KEY THE SETTER DOES NOT FENCE. This is the exact defect that caused the re-plan. The offered aggregate and the fenced aggregate must be the SAME object; a design where they merely happen to agree will drift. Drill (i) must red ON THE REBIND DISPATCH, not on a number comparison.
3. DO NOT FABRICATE A VERSION AND DO NOT INVENT AN ENVIRONMENT NAME (task rail 6). Every offer's version is `versionOf` on a real aggregate; every name comes from the closed roster or from a durable aggregate suffix. An offer carrying an invented version refuses at dispatch in front of an operator — worse than no offer.
4. TWO OFFERS FOR ONE KIND IS THE HAZARD THE FIRST PROBE FOUND. The exclusion is half the fix; per-environment offers WITHOUT it let the card match the unspendable PROJECT-targeted one and the failure reads as a UI bug.
5. WITHHOLDING IS PREREQUISITE-QUALIFIED. `project.activate` gates this kind through the generic prerequisite table (bootstrap-sequence.ts:46). "Nothing withholds it" is false as written and QA will read it literally. Rebinding an already-bound environment remains legitimate (task rail 4) — that is the COMMITTED branch, and it must still offer.
6. THE COMMITTED BRANCH IS EASY TO MISS. After the first bind anywhere, `ledger.kinds.has("deployment.set_target")` sends the generic loop down the COMMITTED path, where only `policy.install` re-offers. Gate the mint on "the generic step is not BLOCKED", not on "it is READY", or rebinding silently loses its affordance again.
7. ORDER MATTERS. Step 2(a) compares an ORDERED tuple list; a Set or an unstable sort makes it flaky. Roster order, then durable-only extras ascending.
8. HOT PATH (the 09-05 affordances incident). The enumeration runs ONCE per readSurface. Do not let it drift inside a per-goal loop.
9. affordance-read.ts is 584 lines and past the cap, and several rows edit it. Add the exclusion clause and the call-and-splice ONLY — no refactor, no reformat, no drive-by comment fixes.
10. NEW FILES ARE UNTRACKED, so `git diff` is blind to them and certifies nothing. The .ts and .js bridge must be restore-proved by sha256 against an out-of-tree backup (global rail 13).
